target_customer: Developers building apps where video is a secondary feature
problem: Handling video upload, transcoding, CDN and playback is hard and costly to maintain for small teams.
business_model: Usage-based API with free tier, a 199 USD per month plan and enterprise pricing

founders.name: Tyler Menezes
prior_employers: Microsoft Research (published papers on machine learning and applied statistics, per YC page)

competitors.name: CameraTag
competitors.what: Webcam video capture and upload service
competitors.traction_then: Called the most active competitor by TechCrunch

competitors.name: Zencoder
competitors.what: Cloud transcoding API developers could wire in themselves

competitors.name: framey
competitors.what: Similar video service that had already shut down

technical_complexity.rationale: Transcoding, device compatibility and CDN delivery behind a clean API were hard for two people but built on existing services.

defensibility.rationale: Zencoder and other transcoding APIs already existed and TechCrunch said developers could stitch the pieces together themselves.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company is listed inactive and framebase.io now redirects to a domain sale page.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in April 2013 said the founders claimed customers it did not name; the pitch was video infrastructure as Twilio did for telephony, with no traction figures published.

branding.name_origin: TapIn.tv pivoted in April 2013 into an infrastructure product and took the name Framebase; no source states why that name was chosen.
branding.domain_note: framebase.io, now parked for sale on GoDaddy

rebrands.why: Pivot from live mobile video app to video infrastructure API

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand beyond the pivot announcement was found.

pivots.why: Crowded live broadcasting market; shift to infrastructure per TechCrunch

outcome_analysis: TapIn.tv entered a crowded live video market and pivoted in April 2013 to Framebase, a video API pitched like Twilio for video. No funding, traction figures or shutdown account were found, and the domain is now for sale, so the cause is not public and pivot_failed is an inference from the pivot then inactive status.
notes: Company site redirects to a GoDaddy sale page (dead). Funding searches found no round; TechCrunch says investor interest existed but no deal was announced. as_of is the pivot date because Framebase did not exist as a product at the batch. Shutdown cause not public. A directory lists activity to 2020, conflicting with the YC inactive status. Competitor dates are about 10 months after the batch. YC page lists four founders against a team size of 2.
